JSON: Name: six_thio_telomerase_stall Title: Single-molecule and biochemical characterization of 6-thio-dGTP–induced telomerase stalling and its effects on telomere maintenance in telomerase-positive cancer cells Short Hypothesis: Incorporation of 6-thio-dGTP by telomerase into the terminal position(s) of telomeric DNA causes telomerase to enter a non-productive stalled complex after translocation, which reduces telomerase repeat addition processivity and induces progressive telomere shortening and dysfunction in telomerase-positive cancer cells with short telomeres. Related Work: Prior approaches to inhibit telomerase include antisense oligonucleotides targeting hTR (e.g., imetelstat) and small molecules that stabilize telomeric G-quadruplexes; nucleoside/nucleotide analog strategies (notably 6-thio-dG/6-thio-dGTP) have shown tumor growth suppression and telomere shortening in cell and animal models. Biochemical studies reported that telomerase can incorporate 6-thio-dGTP and that incorporation reduces further repeat addition in bulk primer-extension assays, but those assays cannot resolve whether inhibition is due to loss of binding, slowed catalysis, altered translocation, or formation of a stalled but DNA-bound complex. TRAP-based cellular assays are insensitive to processivity changes and can miss mechanistic subtleties. Single-molecule telomerase work has characterized RNA–DNA dynamics and recruitment but has not been combined with modified-nucleotide insertion to directly observe stalled states. Limitations in existing work include incomplete specificity profiling against replicative polymerases, lack of single-molecule evidence for enzyme retention after modified-nucleotide incorporation, and insufficient linkage between single-molecule/cell biochemical effects and telomere integrity endpoints. Abstract: Telomerase-mediated telomere maintenance is essential for proliferation of most cancers, and 6-thio-2’-deoxyguanosine (6-thio-dG) is a therapeutic nucleoside reported to cause telomere shortening and tumor suppression. The mechanism by which telomerase insertion of 6-thio-dGTP impairs repeat synthesis and telomere maintenance remains unresolved. We propose an integrated biochemical, single-molecule, and cellular research pipeline to test whether telomerase incorporation of 6-thio-dGTP produces a DNA-bound, non-productive stalled complex after translocation, thereby preventing further repeat addition and driving telomere shortening in telomerase-positive cancer cells. The approach combines quantitative primer-extension processivity assays, single-molecule FRET and optical-tweezer binding/dwell-time measurements, polymerase specificity tests, and cellular telomere-synthesis and integrity assays across cell lines with short and long telomere reserves. Main contributions are: (1) direct single-molecule evidence linking 6-thio-dGTP insertion to stalled telomerase dynamics without dissociation, (2) quantitative separation of effects on catalysis, binding, and translocation, and (3) mapping of sensitivity to telomere length/telomerase status in cells. Expected outcomes include mechanistic validation of 6-thio-dGTP action and experimentally tractable biomarkers predicting cellular sensitivity. Experiments: In vitro biochemical assays: - Telomerase primer-extension: reconstituted human telomerase (FLAG- or Halo-tagged hTERT+hTR) incubated with 32P 5'-endlabeled telomeric primers and dNTPs (24 μM dATP, 29 μM dCTP, 37 μM dTTP, 5.2 μM dGTP) with 6-thio-dGTP titrated (0, 0.1, 1, 5, 10, 100 μM). Measure percent primer extension, processivity R1/2, and IC50 for processivity. Replicates: n>=3 biological. - POT1-TPP1 modulation: repeat primer-extension ±500 nM POT1 and 500 nM TPP1 to test rescue of RAP; quantify change in IC50 and R1/2. - Terminal vs internal 6-thio-dG substrates: synthesize 18-mer telomeric primers with 6-thio-dG at positions within the 4–6 nt alignment region and at internal positions; compare percent extension. - Polymerase specificity: Pol δ holoenzyme (RFC, PCNA, RPA present) primer-extension assays with physiological dNTPs and 6-thio-dGTP replacing dGTP at matched concentrations; measure percent full-length product and insertion probability Pi per template position. Baselines: dGTP control, 6-thio-dGTP substitution, and imetelstat-treated telomerase extract as an orthogonal inhibitor control. Single-molecule assays: - smFRET: reconstituted telomerase labeled LD555 at U42, Cy5-labeled telomeric DNA primers with/without terminal or internal 6-thio-dG; immobilize complexes and acquire time-series at 8.3 Hz. Quantify FRET-state occupancy (high ~0.7, mid 0.4–0.6, low 0.2–0.4), dwell times, fraction of complexes remaining in stalled high-FRET after 15 and 30 min, and transition rates (n >=100 traces per condition). - C-trap optical tweezers: tether telomeric overhangs between beads; measure telomerase binding dwell-time distributions ±6-thio-dGTP and compute cumulative residence-time distributions (fit double-exponential to extract fast/slow off-rates and weighted mean lifetimes). EMSA: Halo-telomerase binding to fluorescence-labeled telomeric substrates with terminal 6-thio-dG vs unmodified; quantify % bound across 0–20 nM enzyme. Cellular assays: cell lines: HCT116 (WT and C50/56A hTR variant), HeLa LT (~27 kb) and HeLa VST (~3.7 kb), U2OS (ALT), RPE1-hTERT and RPE1 control. Treatments: 6-thio-dG at 0, 0.1, 1, 2.5, 5 μM; timepoints 24 h, 72 h, 7 days, 20 days as indicated per assay. Assays and metrics: - Direct telomerase-mediated repeat addition: super-telomerase assay in 293T overexpressing hTERT+hTR; measure new-repeat incorporation via variant-repeat FISH probes (percent nuclei with variant foci, sum intensity). - Telomerase activity in cell extracts: direct primer-extension quantification (percent extension and processivity) from treated vs control cells. - Telomere length distribution: terminal restriction fragment Southern blot; report median telomere length (kb) and distribution shifts. - Telomere integrity: metaphase FISH for signal-free ends and fragile telomeres (count per metaphase); interphase γH2AX–telomere colocalization (TIFs per nucleus). - Proliferation and viability: colony formation efficiency after 9 days; cell counting at indicated timepoints; β-galactosidase senescence fraction. Baselines: untreated, imetelstat-treated, and 6-thio-G-treated where relevant. Ablation/comparison studies: - POT1-TPP1 addition in biochemical assays (presence vs absence). - Terminal vs internal 6-thio-dG on primer substrates. - dGTP:6-thio-dGTP ratio titration (1:0, 1:1, 1:10) in smFRET and biochemical assays. - hTR or hTERT depletion (siRNA) and telomerase-negative U2OS controls. Statistical analysis: report mean ± s.d., use two-tailed t-test or ANOVA with multiple-comparisons correction, state n (biological replicates >=3), and effect sizes for primary endpoints (IC50, fraction stalled, change in median telomere length). Risk Factors and Limitations: Technical failure modes: variability in telomerase reconstitution and labeling efficiency can bias single-molecule readouts; fluorophore photophysics and dye–protein conjugation may alter catalytic behavior; incomplete separation of stalled complexes from inactive enzyme populations may confound interpretation. Data/evaluation biases: cell-line–specific telomere lengths and repair pathway status (MMR, BER) will affect sensitivity; metabolic conversion of 6-thio-dG to other metabolites (6-thio-G, methylated derivatives) in cells may produce off-target effects that mask telomerase-specific outcomes. Specificity and generalization limits: in vitro selectivity versus replicative polymerases may not fully predict in-cell specificity; results may be limited to telomerase-positive tumors and not translate to ALT tumors. Scalability/compute: single-molecule experiments require high-throughput acquisition for robust statistics and may be resource-limited; biochemical kinetic measurements (pre-steady-state) require specialized equipment. Interpretation limits: inability to fully exclude secondary mechanisms (e.g., impaired telomere replication or DNA damage response activation downstream of incorporation) means causality between stalled complexes and long-term telomere shortening may require longitudinal in vivo validation.
